To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
blockchain systems are not yet optimized for data processing workloads, and that the design space for blockchain systems is large, with many opportunities to improve performance.

(1) the performance of blockchain systems is far from satisfactory for data processing tasks, (2) the performance of blockchains is not only limited by the underlying consensus protocol, but also by the design of the distributed ledger and the execution engine, and (3) there is still a lot of space for performance improvement, especially in the design of the ledger.

1) the data processing performance of private block chains can vary by orders of magnitude, 2) the performance gap between blockchain and database can be as large as 1000x, 3) the performance gap is due to both consensus protocol and the underlying storage system, 4) the performance of blockchains is highly dependent on workload characteristics, and 5) the performance gap can be reduced to some extent by optimizing the storage and the consensus protocol.
